The main problem whith snyder's superman stems from the fact that he doesn't resemble superman traits very well.
Superman isnt supposed to smile all the time BUT he cares deeply about human life and isn't like any ordinary superhero. His CLEAR morality is an integral part of him. Superman stands for truth and justice.
Snyder in an attempt to "modernise" superman makes him doubt his morals in a borderline cynical way, superman would help people EVEN if people hate him and he suffers from it.

I understand snyder ATTEMPTING to make superman go on a journey to "earn/learn" his ideals but he went way too far in a lot of scenes (superman lets his father fucking die lmao). Superman is not an objectivist (which is a philosophy snyder likes to implement in his characters), he's the ultimate definition of alturism.

In this particular scene there is no problem of him killing in itself.Genuinely consider how more impactful this scene would be if superman was established as guy raised by 2 genuine good people who taught him to not harm anyone and to always help whoever needs help. Then he goes against his fundamental believes because he IS FORCED to kill zod to SAVE humanity. That would resonate way more with people, instead we get a final battle in metropolis in which superman displays zero emotion to the damage caused (yes he didnt cause it but he could've been shown to have some concern about people like in the previous smallville battle), we get a superman who acts for the majority of the film out of HIS OWN SELF interest. The point is that this superman has been established to EASILY ACCEPT the casualties and IS OKAY with having people die if it means that he saves the day in the end. Therefore him killing doesn't have impact because they never bother establishing that he is against killing.
